programs.name: unif2ti2
programs.purpose: Build uniformly sampled velocity, density, anisotropy, and stiffness grids from layered interfaces.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: UNIF2TI2 - generate a 2-D UNIFormly sampled profile of stiffness

params.name: tfile
params.description: Write the built-in ASCII interface model to this file and exit.

params.name: ninf
params.description: Number of interfaces below the top surface.

params.name: npmax
params.description: Maximum number of points per interface, including the sentinel slot.

params.name: ns
params.description: Vertical smoothing width in samples around interfaces.

params.name: nufile
params.description: Binary float tilt grid in radians; omission selects the VTI calculation.

params.name: method
params.description: Interface interpolation: linear, mono, akima, or spline; selected by first character.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Interface interpolation and stiffness calculations mix float arithmetic with double constants and sqrt; the tilted path calls thom2stiffTI. Partially supplied layer arrays leave remaining elements uninitialized. Smoothing has no bounds checks and can access outside a grid near an edge. Input scanf results are unchecked.
programs.difficulty_reason: It interpolates multiple interfaces, builds layered grids, optionally smooths boundaries, and computes tilted stiffness tensors.

test_cases.description: Generate the built-in model and interpolate it linearly with boundary smoothing.
test_cases.command: unif2ti2 tfile=interfaces.txt && unif2ti2 < interfaces.txt ninf=1 nx=8 nz=64 dx=20 dz=10 method=linear ns=2 vp00=1800,2200 vs00=900,1100 eps00=0.1,0.2 delta00=0.05,0.1

test_cases.description: Use monotonic interface interpolation and a zero tilt grid.
test_cases.command: unif2ti2 tfile=interfaces.txt && vtlvz nt=512 dt=0.004 v0=0 a=0 > tilt.bin && unif2ti2 < interfaces.txt ninf=1 nx=8 nz=64 dx=20 dz=10 method=mono nufile=tilt.bin vp00=1800,2200 vs00=900,1100

programs.license_note: Credits state that Pengfei Cai and Xiaoxiang Wang modified the program, which is based on unif2aniso by John Stockwell.

programs.name: vel2stiff
programs.purpose: Convert velocity, density, anisotropy, and tilt grids into elastic stiffness grids.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: VEL2STIFF - Transforms VELocities, densities, and Thomsen or Sayers

params.name: paramtype
params.description: Use Thomsen parameters when 1; any other value selects the Sayers formula.

params.name: epsfile
params.description: Binary float epsilon grid; omitted values are zero.

params.name: deltafile
params.description: Binary float delta grid; omitted values are zero.

params.name: gammafile
params.description: Binary float gamma grid; omitted values are zero.

params.name: phifile
params.description: Tilt input filename in radians; the selfdoc calls this phi_file, but the code reads phifile.

params.name: phi_file
params.description: Documented tilt filename spelling; not read by the code, which uses phifile.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: The Thomsen branch uses sqrt and float/double mixing; rotation uses double tensor components and casts results to float. The phifile branch reads float-sized bytes directly into a double array, leaving part of the array uninitialized and interpreting bytes as doubles; its result is platform-dependent and invokes undefined behavior.
programs.difficulty_reason: It buffers several model grids and rotates stiffness tensors for two anisotropy parameterizations.

test_cases.description: Convert small isotropic grids with Thomsen parameters.
test_cases.command: vtlvz nt=32 dt=0.004 v0=2000 a=0 > vp.bin && vtlvz nt=32 dt=0.004 v0=1000 a=0 > vs.bin && vtlvz nt=32 dt=0.004 v0=2000 a=0 > rho.bin && vel2stiff nx=4 nz=8 vpfile=vp.bin vsfile=vs.bin rhofile=rho.bin paramtype=1 verbose=0

test_cases.description: Convert anisotropic grids using the Sayers formula.
test_cases.command: vtlvz nt=32 dt=0.004 v0=2200 a=0 > vp.bin && vtlvz nt=32 dt=0.004 v0=1000 a=0 > vs.bin && vtlvz nt=32 dt=0.004 v0=1900 a=0 > rho.bin && vtlvz nt=32 dt=0.004 v0=0.1 a=0 > anis.bin && vel2stiff nx=4 nz=8 vpfile=vp.bin vsfile=vs.bin rhofile=rho.bin epsfile=anis.bin deltafile=anis.bin gammafile=anis.bin paramtype=0 verbose=0

programs.license_note: The header cites Sayers' 1995 Geophysics paper and credits the Sayers-parameter extension to Stig-Kyrre Foss.

programs.name: velconv
programs.purpose: Convert binary velocity and time-depth functions between time and depth representations.

params.name: intype
params.description: Input function type: vintt, vrmst, vintz, zt, tz, otherz, or othert under the code's otherfile rules.

params.name: outtype
params.description: Output function type: vintt, vrmst, vintz, zt, tz, otherz, or othert under the code's otherfile rules.

params.name: nt
params.default: computed: nz if supplied, otherwise input file size in floats

params.name: nz
params.default: computed: nt if supplied, otherwise input file size in floats

params.name: nx
params.description: Number of input vectors; negative processes until EOF.

params.name: otherfile
params.description: Optional binary float property grid; when set, both types must be otherz or othert.

programs.float_sensitive_notes: Conversions accumulate float sums, invert sampled functions with yxtoxy, and use sqrt and float/double expressions. in_vintt tests uninitialized zt elements instead of the input velocities. Extrapolation loops lack bounds checks for some sampling ranges. The otherfile interpolation uses zt or tz as both input and output coordinates, and otherz is accepted without otherfile. Standard input is unconditionally seeked to its beginning, so a regular file is needed.
programs.difficulty_reason: It buffers vectors and uses numerical integration, inverse interpolation, extrapolation, and several conversion paths.

test_cases.description: Convert interval velocity in depth to RMS velocity in time.
test_cases.command: vtlvz nt=64 dt=0.004 v0=2000 a=0 > velocity.bin && velconv < velocity.bin > rms.bin intype=vintz outtype=vrmst nz=64 nt=64 dz=4 dt=0.004 nx=1

test_cases.description: Convert RMS velocity in time to depth as a function of time.
test_cases.command: vtlvz nt=64 dt=0.004 v0=2000 a=0.2 > velocity.bin && velconv < velocity.bin > depth.bin intype=vrmst outtype=zt nt=64 nz=64 dt=0.004 dz=4 nx=1

test_cases.description: Convert an additional property from depth to time.
test_cases.command: vtlvz nt=64 dt=0.004 v0=2000 a=0 > velocity.bin && vtlvz nt=64 dt=0.004 v0=1800 a=0.1 > property.bin && velconv < velocity.bin > property_time.bin intype=otherz outtype=othert otherfile=property.bin nz=64 nt=64 dz=4 dt=0.004 nx=1

programs.name: vtlvz
programs.purpose: Generate velocity as a function of time for a linear velocity-versus-depth model.
programs.selfdoc_first_line: VTLVZ -- Velocity as function of Time for Linear V(Z);
programs.float_sensitive_notes: Time is accumulated in float, while exp and the division by 2.0 use double arithmetic; transcendental results can vary by platform.
programs.difficulty_reason: It generates one float vector using a direct exponential formula.

test_cases.command: vtlvz nt=64 dt=0.004 v0=2000 a=0 > velocity.bin

test_cases.description: Generate velocity with a positive gradient.
test_cases.command: vtlvz nt=128 dt=0.002 v0=1500 a=0.8 > velocity.bin
